# A1b — Does the constructed surplus cohere with the measured load?

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_a1b.py`: a test in service of a hypothesis, what it would need and what it could show. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

**Not in the hypothesis register.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-REGISTER">This test is not one of the register's hypotheses: it serves [A1](../hypodrafts/A1.md "Danish land-based nitrogen load"), and is more specific than it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-REGISTER "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-QUESTION">*The field surplus is a construction; the stream and estuary nitrogen are measured, the stream series only where it is gauged. Do they move together, and does the relation hold still?*</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-QUESTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

Companion to [`A1.md`](A1.md), which drafts the residual-growth test on the published attribution. This one tests the **coupling**, not the accounting.

---

## The observable consequence

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-NORMS">`markoverskud`, the field surplus, is built from coefficients as well as counts: manure nitrogen from livestock numbers times the norms in force, crop nitrogen from the editions of the feed tables. It can move when a coefficient moves, with no change in any field. SR120 records two changes on known dates:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-NORMS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-1999">**1999** — the nitrogen norm was cut [10](../SOURCES.md#F-e098799d4c)%, lowering the nitrogen *quota* by about [40,000](../SOURCES.md#F-4fa2a56883) t N, while grass norms changed and raised it by about [15,000](../SOURCES.md#F-2b35b5362f) t N a year; SR120 calls the result a *"spring"* — a step — in the compiled quotas.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-1999 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-1999-QUOTA">The quota is what a farm may apply, set from crop norms; it is not a term of the surplus, and a cut in it can change what is applied. Whether the surplus steps at 1999, and by how much, is what the test measures.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-1999-QUOTA "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-2012">**2012** — the method for nutrients removed at harvest changed from dry-matter yield to feed units for roughage crops, and SR120 records that its *phosphorus* net-input figures *"er steget lidt ift. de tidligere opgørelser"* — rose against the earlier reports: a revision between vintages, stated for phosphorus. Its effect on nitrogen is not stated there.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-2012 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-TEST">**If the constructed series steps at 1999, or at another date where a coefficient changed, and the measured series does not, the surplus↔load relation must break at that date. The size of the break measures the construction's non-physical component.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-TEST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-FALSIFY">**Falsified if** the relation is stable across 1999 — either the norm change passed through to what was applied and to the load, or the step is small relative to the noise; either way the construction carries no spurious discontinuity there.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-FALSIFY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-CONFIRM">**Confirmed if** a regression fitted before 1999 mispredicts after it, in the direction and roughly the magnitude the norm change implies.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-CONFIRM "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Why this test and not a correlation

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-WHOLE">SR353 states its relation between the national field surplus and the normalised diffuse load *"for perioden som helhed"* — for the period as a whole, over a series it computes from 1990: one relation across the 1999 change. A correlation over the whole period cannot distinguish a real coupling from a coupling plus a shared administrative step; a discontinuity test can, because only one of the two series should step.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-WHOLE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-SIDEWAYS">This is the residual-growth logic applied sideways. There, a part is moved out of a leftover and the arithmetic must close. Here, a part is moved *into* the construction by an administrative decision, and the measurement must **not** move.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-SIDEWAYS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Data

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-D-SURPLUS">**Annual national field surplus, 1990 onward**: SR120's Bilag 1, *Markbalancer for 1990-2013*, in a public report whose text extracts (pinned here).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-D-SURPLUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-D-GAP">**Surplus and diffuse load per catchment**: no such series has been read here; SR353 gives the national relation, and SR120 balances for its agricultural monitoring catchments, not for the catchments of coastal waters.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-D-GAP "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-D-ESTUARY">**Measured nitrogen in the sea**: the held ODA water-chemistry extract carries total nitrogen on [190,473](../SOURCES.md#F-a17c9263d9) rows — the independent terminal series.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-D-ESTUARY "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-D-STREAM">**Stream nitrogen where it is gauged**: SR353 computes the national load from [209](../SOURCES.md#F-b6474e2555) coastal stream stations and a model for the rest, so it is measured on the gauged fraction only.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-D-STREAM "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-CLASSES">The surplus is a **norm product**; the load is **hybrid** — measured on the gauged fraction, model output on the rest, since the ungauged part is DK-QNP output whose input is the surplus itself (class `7` in [the taxonomy of data-stream errors](https://github.com/Jjokulian/statistical-methods#7b-rate-a-data-stream-by-the-errors-it-can-contain)). **Use the gauged fraction only**, or the test is partly circular by construction. Measured nitrogen in the sea does not pass through the surplus at all.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-CLASSES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The null, which is not zero

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-NULL">A break-point test finds breaks in autocorrelated series with no breaks in them. The null must be **matched-autocorrelation surrogates with no step**, and the reported quantity is where the observed break sits in that distribution — not a p-value against independence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-NULL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

Two further controls:

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-PLACEBO">**Placebo dates.** Fit the same break test at every year 1993–2006. If 1999 is not distinguished from its neighbours, there is no step to find.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-PLACEBO "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-STRAT">**Gauged-fraction stratification.** The circular component scales with the modelled share, so the effect should be strongest where a catchment's modelled share is largest and weakest where it is smallest.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-STRAT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What a result would and would not license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-WOULD">**Would**: a number for how much of the surplus series is administrative, on a stated date, with the measured series as reference.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-WOULD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-WOULDNOT">**Would not**: anything about whether agriculture causes hypoxia. This tests the coherence of two series, one constructed and one measured. A clean break at 1999 would say the construction carries a bookkeeping jump — not that the underlying load did not fall.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-WOULDNOT "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-A1B-DECLINE">Whether it fell is a separate question, which DCE answer from the measured record: SR353 puts the reduction in nitrogen supply from land to the coast since the start of its series at [51](../SOURCES.md#F-f3813ac6c6)%, calculated on discharge-weighted mean annual concentrations. **Both things can be true: the construction partly administrative, and the decline real.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-A1B-DECLINE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
